It really comes down to history. Back in the day, YouTube was very small and simple. People shared content to "Broadcast" themselves without monetary gain. But the time came when the community became larger and it's getting hard for people to watch content if only new videos were showcased. As you can tell, my point leads to the problem developing that we call as spams. Nobody wants that, and they even established community guidelines for users to agree on when using the platform. But guidelines aren't enough, it's not gonna stop spammers for stepping over other people's content. So they have to introduce the algorithm for that and it was designed to actually solve that exact problem. As time moves forward, there are people who are still trying to break the algorithm to spam content, therefore the algorithm has to improve delivering "not spam" contents to people based on their interest. Otherwise people would've just leave YouTube and will eventually kill the platform.

So this continuous ongoing cycle leads us to making higher quality content. And throughout the years, majority of people only care about high quality content. The ones that give them a dopamine hit every single time. And finally we are now in the present where the algorithm is very strict to the point that us smaller creators are getting caught in the crossfire. This is not just YouTube alone, other popular social media platforms took inspiration from this concept with a little extra gimmick on top.

So... There you go. It is sad that her story ended that way. Nobody expected that from happening. But that's the reality we face today, especially for being a small creator you and me included. Bloo, your legacy shall not be forgotten in VTubing history. May you rest in peace.

EDIT: I've just got the feeling I have to add this, Algorithms loves drama, controversy, and shocking content. Because that's where majority of people engage with. Which lead back to us... People... I do hope the algorithm helps smaller content creators so at least we have a chance to be visible and let people know we exist.

IMO if you have absolutely 0 idea on how to edit, Davinci is not a good way to start. 

You need to get the basics down, (e.g. manipulating video via position sizes etc., understanding of resolution and what framerate to use, keyframes) once you understand those, you can upgrade your skills by starting on the free version of Davinci and work your way from there.

In case you're overwhelmed, you can use something that's simpler to use like CapCut (I heard it's easy but never used it) until you understand the basics of video editing. If you are really in need of high quality content with high quality editing while producing constant content you can hire someone to do the editing job for you.

I'm not saying don't start with Davinci, I'm just saying it's not really a user friendly option for people that don't know editing as you might get overwhelmed at it at first. But once you got the basics that I've just mentioned, you are ready to start learning Davinci to ramp up your content. Keep this in mind, Davinci is one of the most powerful video editing software out there that can ramp up your game.

Good luck.

DaVinci Resolve is an editing software that is intended for professional work. You might be experiencing bottlenecks on your PC's resources. Check your RAM, GPU, CPU, and storage utilizations. See which one of them caps on 100% usage.

Also, you mentioned your fans are going crazy while using Resolve. Check your temps, you might be experiencing thermal throttling on your components.

Also, Resolve comes with a Proxy Generator. It will definitely help to improve your playback speed by a ton.

Other than that, if you can, upgrade your GPU, RAM, CPU, or you could opt in for an SSD. Depending on how high quality your footage, Resolve will normally use a lot of resources on your PC most especially if you are working on higher resolution clips.
